title: Juniper and the Compass
premise: In 1848, in the garrison town of Vellamouth, apprentice mapmaker Rosalind Okonkwo secretly completes the atlas his murdered master died protecting—an atlas whose marginalia records the names of every family the Crown has displaced. When the army requisitions the town and seizes the census ledger to decide who may board the last evacuation ship, Rosalind realizes the atlas's hidden names can expose the requisition as a land-grab disguised as rescue. Torn between his sister Adaeze, his ailing mentor's widow, and the daughter of the general overseeing the evictions, he must smuggle the atlas to a reformist printer before the ship sails. In the end he wins justice for the town at the cost of his own berth, giving his place to a stranger's child—and choosing exile over safety, armed with the truth and the woman who helped him carry it.
about_author: Isandro Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial survey maps before turning to fiction. He writes from a coastal cottage, where he keeps an unfinished 19th-century atlas on his desk as a reminder that every line on a map was drawn by someone with something to gain.

chapters.title: The Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Rosalind Okonkwo works late in dead Master Hollis's map room, finishing the atlas Hollis died for, tracing coastlines by candlelight. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: quiet devotion shadowed by grief; he believes history happens elsewhere, to other people.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Lives
chapters.summary: Rosalind delivers survey maps to the town clerk and glimpses the census ledger—every name in Vellamouth, including his sister Adaeze's. He notices soldiers measuring the harbor. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: first unease, the sense of being watched by paperwork.

chapters.title: Adaeze Counts the Boats
chapters.summary: Adaeze, a dockworker, counts troop transports anchoring overnight and warns Rosalind that something is coming. He dismisses her fears. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: protective frustration between siblings; her pragmatism against his abstraction.

chapters.title: The Widow's Warning
chapters.summary: Hollis's widow, Margaret, shows Rosalind a letter her husband hid inside the atlas's binding—a list of displaced families from three towns, all erased from official record. POV: Margaret. Emotional beat: dread inherited from the dead; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: At dawn, redcoats seal the harbor. A proclamation: Vellamouth is requisitioned for 'sanitary necessity'; one ship will carry a limited number of residents; the ledger decides who goes. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of ordinary life.

chapters.title: Names Become Currency
chapters.summary: The town learns its fate is alphabetical and arbitrary. Neighbors bribe, forge, and betray for ledger priority. Rosalind sees the clerk alter entries. POV: ensemble via Rosalind. Emotional beat: horror at how quickly neighbors become competitors.

chapters.title: The General's Daughter
chapters.summary: Rosalind is summoned to survey the fort and meets Captain Elowen Vance, the general's daughter, who corrects his maps with unsettling precision—and quiet shame about the eviction. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: wary attraction tangled with resentment.

chapters.title: What Hollis Died For
chapters.summary: Margaret reveals Hollis was killed after refusing to surrender the atlas to government surveyors; the marginalia names are evidence of a patterned land-grab. POV: Margaret. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve; passing the torch.

chapters.title: A Berth for One
chapters.summary: The family receives notice: only ONE Okonkwo name appears on the sailing list—Adaeze's. Rosalind and Margaret are excluded. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: guilt and fury; love turned into arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Choice Begins
chapters.summary: Adaeze refuses to leave without Rosalind; Margaret urges her to go anyway. Rosalind secretly resolves to win berths for all three by exposing the ledger's fraud. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes—justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: Forging Coastlines
chapters.summary: Rosalind uses his cartographic access to copy the ledger's altered pages during a fort survey, nearly caught by Sergeant Bray. Elowen covers for him without explanation. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration; first act of resistance.

chapters.title: Elowen's Doubt
chapters.summary: Elowen confronts her father about the 'sanitary' fiction; he shows her orders from above and tells her loyalty is the only mercy she'll be permitted. POV: Elowen. Emotional beat: duty cracking under conscience.

chapters.title: The Printer in the Marsh
chapters.summary: Margaret leads Rosalind through marshland to Tobias Finch, a reformist printer exiled after publishing Hollis's earlier findings. Finch agrees to print the atlas's evidence—if Rosalind can get the original out of the sealed map room. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: hope with teeth; allies found in unlikely places.

chapters.title: Curfew Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Daily life under occupation: ration lines, informants, a neighbor deported for a forged stamp. Adaeze organizes dockworkers to slow the loading of army cargo. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: solidarity kindling; small defiance compounding.

chapters.title: Bray Suspects
chapters.summary: Sergeant Bray searches the map room and finds Rosalind's copied pages missing from sequence. He sets a trap: a false order luring Rosalind back at night. POV: Bray. Emotional beat: cold menace; the hunter's patience.

chapters.title: Night Survey
chapters.summary: Rosalind walks into Bray's trap but escapes through the chart drawers and rooftops, injuring his hand. Elowen finds him bleeding and, instead of arresting him, binds the wound. POV: Rosalind/Elowen alternating. Emotional beat: the moment love stops being deniable.

chapters.title: Two Maps of the Same Town
chapters.summary: Elowen gives Rosalind her father's private survey—the real plan: a naval depot, the town never to be returned. She asks nothing in return. POV: Elowen. Emotional beat: betrayal of blood for principle; love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: The Widow's Bargain
chapters.summary: Margaret offers Bray the atlas's location in exchange for three berths—stalling him while Rosalind moves the real atlas. POV: Margaret. Emotional beat: sacrifice dressed as treachery; courage in an old woman's calm.

chapters.title: What the Margins Hold
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Hollis's final weeks, gathering names from refugees, knowing the cost. His voice frames why memory itself is resistance. POV: Hollis (via letters). Emotional beat: elegy; the dead instructing the living.

chapters.title: Loading Day
chapters.summary: The ship takes on cargo first; passengers learn boarding is postponed indefinitely. Rumor says the ship may never sail at all—the eviction is permanent. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: despair curdling into rage on the docks.

chapters.title: The Riot at the Gate
chapters.summary: Denied boarding, crowds surge the quay; soldiers fire over their heads. Adaeze pulls a child from a trampling and is arrested for incitement. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: chaos, then the sickening quiet after.

chapters.title: Cell and Compass
chapters.summary: Rosalind visits Adaeze in custody; she tells him to stop trying to save everyone and finish the atlas. He realizes the book, not the ship, is the true escape route. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: clarity through helplessness.

chapters.title: Elowen's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: General Vance discovers Elowen's leaked survey. He offers her a choice: testify that Rosalind is a spy, or be court-martialed alongside him. POV: Elowen. Emotional beat: the noose tightening around love itself.

chapters.title: The Forged Chart
chapters.summary: Rosalind plants a decoy atlas—beautifully wrong—in the map room. Bray seizes it triumphantly. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: gambler's calm masking fear; outdrawing the state with penmanship.

chapters.title: Trial of Ink
chapters.summary: A summary tribunal charges Rosalind with sedition based on the decoy's 'coded' annotations. Elowen, forced to attend, watches her father preside. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the law revealed as theater; justice visibly absent.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Elowen takes the stand and, instead of condemning Rosalind, reads aloud the real displacement figures from her father's own survey. The courtroom erupts. POV: Elowen. Emotional beat: the novel's moral hinge—duty redefined at personal ruin.

chapters.title: The General's Fall
chapters.summary: Vance, exposed, tries to burn the evidence and blame rioters; Bray, realizing he was given a forgery, turns on his superior to save himself. POV: Bray/Vance. Emotional beat: power devouring its own; corruption's cascade.

chapters.title: Fire in the Map Room
chapters.summary: The real atlas is nearly lost when Vance's men torch the archive; Rosalind and Margaret salvage it through the smoke, Margaret burned and broken. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: grief and urgency fused; the cost becomes flesh.

chapters.title: Last Berth
chapters.summary: One berth remains on the finally-departing ship. Adaeze, released in the chaos, is entitled to it—but a dockside stranger's injured child has no name on any list. Rosalind makes the choice the title promises. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the climax of sacrifice; love measured in what is given away.

chapters.title: Sailing Without Her
chapters.summary: Adaeze refuses the berth too, giving it to the child, and chooses to stay and rebuild. The siblings part reconciled, neither exiled by the other. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: bittersweet grace; family redefined beyond survival.

chapters.title: The Printing of Truth
chapters.summary: Finch prints the atlas's evidence overnight; by dawn, pamphlets naming every displaced family circulate through three counties. Clergy, merchants, and a sympathetic magistrate take up the cause. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the turn—truth gaining mass and momentum.

chapters.title: Inquiry
chapters.summary: A royal commission arrives; Elowen testifies formally, stripped of rank but unrepentant. Vance is recalled in disgrace. POV: Elowen. Emotional beat: vindication without victory's sweetness; institutional justice arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Restitution
chapters.summary: Berths are reissued; the requisition rescinded pending inquiry. Families return to marked houses. Rosalind redraws the town map with every restored name inscribed. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: repair as an act of drawing; the mapmaker restoring what maps erased.

chapters.title: Bray's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Bray, facing charges, trades testimony about the land syndicate behind the requisition. Margaret, recovering, watches him led away and feels not triumph but fatigue. POV: Margaret. Emotional beat: closure without catharsis; the long cost of justice.

chapters.title: The Empty Frame
chapters.summary: Rosalind hangs Hollis's portrait in the rebuilt map room and takes apprentices—including dock children Adaeze sends him. Knowledge becomes inheritance. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: continuity; grief transmuted into teaching.

chapters.title: An Offer of Exile
chapters.summary: The Crown offers Rosalind a post mapping new territories—the same empire, better pay. He recognizes the invitation to be complicit politely. He declines. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: temptation refused; the theme resolved in a single signature withheld.

chapters.title: Where the Compass Points
chapters.summary: Elowen, dismissed from the army, asks Rosalind to teach her surveying so they can map the coastline independently—for the fishermen, not the admiralty. POV: Elowen. Emotional beat: love choosing a shared vocation over safety or status.

chapters.title: Departure Tide
chapters.summary: The last transport sails empty of Vellamouth's people. On the quay, the community that resisted stands together as the fog lifts off the water. POV: ensemble via Adaeze. Emotional beat: collective exhale; the town belonging to itself again.

chapters.title: The Finished Atlas
chapters.summary: Rosalind completes the final plate: Vellamouth, drawn whole, with Hollis's marginalia printed openly beneath it. He adds one line of his own. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: fulfillment; the master's work and the apprentice's faith made one.

chapters.title: Juniper and the Compass
chapters.summary: Years later, Rosalind and Elowen's schoolhouse teaches children to read maps critically. A juniper tree grows over Hollis's grave; beneath the atlas's dedication, his chosen line: 'For those the ledger forgot.' POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: peace earned, legacy planted, story closed.
